Patch 0.38.0 (Friendships database schema)

  • A persistent friendship table is live: The friendships MongoDB collection stores directed relationships with requester_id, addressee_id, and status fields.
  • Mutual-accept model: A request must be accepted before either side sees the other in their friend list; duplicate requests in either direction are blocked at the DB layer.
  • Six CRUD methods: SendFriendRequest, AcceptFriendRequest, DeclineFriendRequest, RemoveFriend, GetFriends, and GetPendingRequests cover the full friendship lifecycle.
  • Regression coverage: Added Go DB schema, indexes, CRUD methods, and the 0.38.0 release state.

Patch 0.37.4 (Social status enforcement and auto-transitions)

  • Busy blocks party invites: The server now rejects party invitations sent to a player whose status is Busy, and the inviter receives a clear explanation.
  • Dungeon entry automatically sets In Run: When your party enters a dungeon, the server sets every member's status to In Run and broadcasts the updated roster — no manual update required.
  • Respawn and Recall automatically restore Available: Returning to the overworld via respawn or recall reverts your status from In Run to Available and triggers a fresh roster broadcast.
  • Busy is respected throughout: If you explicitly chose Busy before entering a dungeon, the server will not override it — on entry or on return.
  • Regression coverage: Added server and client coverage for busy invite blocking, automatic in-run transitions, available revert logic, and the 0.37.4 release state.

Patch 0.37.3 (Proactive social-status broadcast)

  • Social status changes are now visible without reopening the window: When any player changes their status, a fresh roster is pushed to every open Social window within the same server tick.
  • Previously the Social window only refreshed on open: Stale statuses no longer require manually closing and reopening the panel to see updates.
  • Regression coverage: Added server coverage for proactive Social list broadcast and the 0.37.3 release state.

Patch 0.37.2 (Party-member highlight)

  • Party members are visually distinct in the world: A teal ring now appears around the character model of every player in your party — no need to open the Party panel to recognise your group.
  • The ring updates automatically: Joining a party, leaving, or another member disconnecting refreshes the ring for all party members within the same state tick.
  • Existing party and combat flows are unchanged: The ring is a visual overlay; no combat, reward, or party management behavior was modified.
  • Regression coverage: Added client coverage for party ring lifecycle, mesh replacement, and the 0.37.2 release state.

Patch 0.37.1 (Party persistence across disconnects)

  • Party membership now survives a disconnect: Your party ID is stored in the database and rejoined automatically on login if the party is still active when you return.
  • Expired members are cleaned up honestly: If your resume window closes before you reconnect, you are removed from the party at that point rather than silently holding a dead slot.
  • Regression coverage: Added Go unit tests for party rejoin, expired-member cleanup, and the 0.37.1 release state.

Patch 0.37.0 (Party and social-status proto fields)

  • Party ID and social status now ride the binary state stream: party_id and social_status are added as first-class fields in state.proto; both the Go server and JS client are regenerated from the updated schema.
  • State updates are leaner and more reliable: Party membership and social presence are now delta-compressed alongside position, health, and all other entity fields instead of riding a separate JSON path.
  • Regression coverage: Added 11 Go tests for proto encoding, snapshot diffing, and the 0.37.0 release state.

Patch 0.36.3 (Connection-state HUD indicator)

  • A connection banner now appears when the game is reconnecting: A pill indicator at the top-center of the screen shows "Reconnecting…" (amber, pulsing) or "Connection lost" (red) so you always know the connection state without guessing.
  • The banner disappears automatically on successful resume: Once the session resumes, the indicator hides itself — normal play has no persistent overlay.
  • NetworkManager fires connection-state change events: onConnectionStateChange is called with 'reconnecting', 'connected', or 'lost' at each transition and is wired to UIManager.setConnectionState().
  • Regression coverage: Added UIManager setConnectionState tests covering all three states and the missing-element guard. Added NetworkManager tests covering each state-change path.

Patch 0.36.2 (Client-side reconnect loop)

  • Transient disconnects no longer reload the page: NetworkManager now retries with exponential back-off (up to 5 attempts, starting at 1 s) instead of calling window.location.reload().
  • Session resume is replayed on reconnect: When a new WebSocket opens, the stored resume token is sent automatically; a successful server ack refreshes the token in localStorage.
  • Unrecoverable disconnects show the login screen: Once all retry attempts are exhausted or the server rejects the token, the login panel is restored and the stale token is cleared.
  • Regression coverage: Added 18 NetworkManager tests covering the back-off schedule, resume-token handshake, server rejection, and destroy-timer cancel paths.

Patch 0.36.0 (Server-side session resume)

  • Your character stays in the world during a brief disconnect: The server now issues a cryptographic resume token at login and keeps your entity in a "disconnected" state for up to 5 minutes instead of removing it immediately.
  • Rejoining with a valid token restores your session in place: MsgResumeSession validates the token, rebinds your entity, issues a fresh token, and resends full player state — no re-login required.
  • Expired or double-used tokens are rejected cleanly: Tokens are single-use and expire after the resume window; a 30-second sweep goroutine removes entities whose window has closed.
  • Regression coverage: Added 9 Go unit tests for the world disconnect / resume lifecycle.

Patch 0.35.0 (Remote smoothing hardening)

  • Remote motion is more stable: Nearby remote-player interpolation now clamps frame spikes to the latest server target instead of overshooting past it.
  • Remote facing is safer: Remote rotation smoothing uses the same clamped interpolation window so large frame deltas settle cleanly on server-facing intent.
  • Local authority stays unchanged: The fix only affects remote actor presentation and does not change local movement, combat, party, chat, trading, or dungeon-entry behavior.
  • Regression coverage: Added client coverage for remote interpolation frame-spike handling and the 0.35.0 release state.
